title: Turing reducibility and degrees of unsolvability

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: §15.2, printed/PDF pp. 64–66: Turing reducibility and equivalence, the computable least degree, and the binary join; version 2024-02-25

summary: Compare membership problems through oracle programs, form Turing degrees, and combine two degrees by their least upper bound.
abstract: Knowing how to answer a membership problem lets us answer its opposite by reversing the answer, even when a single computable translation cannot express that use of the information. Turing reducibility compares problems by allowing a fixed program to compute one set's membership answers using queries about another set. Problems that can answer one another's questions belong to the same Turing degree. All computable membership problems form the least degree, while the halting problem has a degree strictly above it. Storing two sets in the even and odd positions of a new set combines their information. Its degree is the least one sufficient to decide both original problems, giving a binary join in the order of degrees.
